I didn't change anything: `packages/db/src/emails.ts` already contains the full contract the spec describes.

The spec says the change "adds, removes and renames no exports, and no signature changes". Every name it lists is already exported from the seam with the stated signatures and values:
- `createProfileStore`
- `createEmailStore`
- `USERNAME_MIN_LENGTH = 3`
- `USERNAME_MAX_LENGTH = 30`
- `ProvenEmail`, `EmailStore`, `UsernameResult` and `UserProfileStore`

The fake the tests are told to use, `createFakeEmailDb`, is already exported from `packages/db/test/fake-email-db.ts`.

The only thing that changes is the hyphen strip inside `toHandleBase`, which the spec requires to stay private, and rewriting it is the implementation's job. Replacing it with `throw new Error("not implemented");` would break `suggest`, which is an export whose body has to stay as it is, so I left the file exactly as it was.

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors, and the existing suite still passes (105 tests, 0 failures).

Exported names added: none.

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite as one file: `packages/db/test/trim-hyphens-confirmed.test.ts`. It type-checks with no errors and runs, but **every test passes now instead of failing**. The `toHandleBase` in this checkout doesn't throw `not implemented`; it still has the original `replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")`. Since the spec requires output identical to the regex for every input, passing against the old code is consistent, but it means these tests can't tell a fixed version from the unfixed one.

The slow-input problem does show up, as timing only. Three of the tests that use a 100,000-hyphen run between two characters each take about 3.5 seconds against the current regex; the others finish in milliseconds. The spec rules out timing assertions, so nothing fails on that. The developer will see a drop in run time when the linear version lands, not a test going from failing to passing.

**What's covered:** each of the 18 scenarios has two tests, a happy path and one boundary case. Every test name starts with its scenario key, from `[happy-1]` to `[happy-4]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-10]`, `[unhappy-1]` to `[unhappy-3]` and `[concurrency-1]`. Some of the boundary cases are my own additions on top of the spec's examples, for example:
- A run of 30 leading hyphens before a 3-letter name.
- 28 letters followed by `---`, so the trailing hyphens cross the 30-character limit and must be trimmed before truncation.
- A long run mixing hyphens and `.` characters (which become hyphens) on both sides of the name.
- A long hyphen run in among parallel calls.
- A 30-character name that is already taken, which forces the random-suffix fallback onto a shortened stem.

**Conventions:** it follows the style of `profile.test.ts`: `node:test` with `assert/strict`, flat top-level tests, and the `createFakeEmailDb` fake with the same `user()` helper and fixed dates. The random-suffix tests check only the shape of the handle (`/^dana-[0-9a-f]{6}$/`), because the suffix comes from `crypto.randomUUID` and the interface gives no way to fix it.

I changed nothing else in the repository.

36 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in `packages/db/test/hidden-trim-hyphens-confirmed/`, but one of your rules can't be met: **these tests don't fail against the interface as it stands.** The seam has no `not implemented` body. `toHandleBase` in `packages/db/src/emails.ts` still uses the old `replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")` strip. The spec defines the right output as "exactly what it returns today", so any test that follows the spec passes against that code. The official command reports 60 of 60 passing, in about 46 s. The time goes on the 100,000-hyphen inputs, where the old regex is quadratic. Only a timing assertion could tell the old and new code apart, and the spec rules that out. The suite does its job against a new implementation, but it can't be run against the stub as intended.

**What I checked:**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors.
- In a scratchpad copy I swapped in an index-walking trim. All 60 hidden tests and the 35 public ones passed, in about 0.5 s.
- I then ran broken versions of the trim against the suite. Each one fails hidden tests:

| Broken version | Hidden tests failed | Public tests failed |
|---|---|---|
| strips only one hyphen at each end | 49 | 17 |
| truncates before trimming | 19 | 10 |
| collapses interior hyphen runs | 22 | 7 |
| returns `user` for an empty stem | 17 | 7 |
| trims again after truncating | 12 | 5 |
| also trims `_` | 10 | 3 |
| scans at most 1,000 leading characters | 4 | 2 |
| replaces characters before lowercasing | 1 | not run |

**What the suite covers:**
- **Every scenario key:** happy 1–4, boundary 1–10, unhappy 1–3 and concurrency-1. Each public test has at least one extension, named in a comment above it.
- **Exhaustive comparisons:** some tests compare `suggest` against a copy of the old regex function. They cover every short input over small character sets, plus grids of leading hyphens, trailing hyphens and interior runs around the 30-character limit.
- **Lowercasing order:** one test uses the Kelvin sign (`\u212A`), which lowercases to `k`. It's the only test that catches an implementation which replaces characters before lowercasing.
- **Collisions:** counters and the random fallback on padded stems (`jo-user2`), on the `-user` stem, and on a cut-off stem ending in `-`. A taken untrimmed form doesn't count as a collision.
- **Long inputs:** runs of 100,000–250,000 hyphens, runs on one side only, runs made of replaced characters, and runs after a name that already fills the 30 characters.

Nothing outside that folder was changed. The compiled `dist-test` output is git-ignored.

60 tests, in 4 files.

Open in the spec: none
